title: FREAK: A Fine-grained Hallucination Evaluation Benchmark for Advanced MLLMs
claim: Benchmark data is built through a staged generate, edit, and verify procedure that turns text prompts into counter-commonsense images and questions.
layout: 3 colored panels, numbered stages, mixed flow; worked example threaded through all stages
description: Three color-coded boxes show a data-generation pipeline with a single running example, a traffic light. Panel 1 (green, top-left) takes a noun list and object name, builds a prompt instruction, passes it to an LLM (GPT icon and head-with-gears icon), and outputs a CCS content JSON file. Panel 3 (blue, top-right) shows CCS images and JSON feeding a second prompt instruction. The LLM then writes a question, and filtering and verification produce the FREAK database. Panel 2 (red, bottom, widest) shows JSON going into an image-generation model that produces a normal street image. An editing model then makes the counter-commonsense image, with the traffic light swapped and boxed in red. Black arrows connect the stages. Large photos in the bottom row draw the eye first.
caption: Generation pipeline of FREAK, including a three-step generation paradigm. We first prompt LLMs to generate CCS content for later stages, next we use image genration model and editing model to generate CCS image. Finally we filter and verify the generated data to form FREAK benchmark. In this example, we exhibit the generation process of \enquote{Traffic Light}. The generated image shows the positions of the red and green lights swapped, incorrectly with red at the bottom and green at the top, which violates both commonsense and the traffic regulations of various countries.
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) suffer from hallucinations. Existing hallucination evaluation benchmarks are often limited by over-simplified tasks leading to saturated metrics, or insufficient diversity that fails to adequately assess the hallucination extent in state-of-the-art multimodal models. To address this gap, we propose FREAK, a comprehensive multimodal benchmark designed for fine-grained hallucination assessment in MLLMs. Through high-quality photorealistic images featuring fine-grained counter-commonsense edits, FREAK innovatively evaluates hallucination phenomena in detailed visual perception of MLLMs. Extensive experiments on FREAK show severe hallucination issues in SOTA models regarding detailed visual perception. To enable deeper investigation, we curate a controlled subset to indirectly evaluate the model's ability to perceive target detailed information. Through systematic evaluation of prevailing Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting techniques within this task, we reveal critical insights regarding hallucination patterns and model reasoning processes.
